text:
Kai: Heads up — infra is planning a firewall policy flip in eu-west-2 tonight (deny-by-default for pod-egress). I think it will affect our GPU node onboarding path and could cause a provisioning spike/cold-starts. Can security postpone or carve exceptions?
Marta: Thanks for flagging. Which specific flows are you worried about? node bootstrap, container image pull, or control-plane callbacks?
Kai: Primarily node bootstrap + image pull + IAM token exchange to KMS for disk key unwrap. If any of those get blocked, new GPU nodes stay in Pending and traffic piles up -> burst of prewarmed replacements later.
Oliver: If nodes stuck Pending we see capacity debt and scheduler will siphon traffic to other regions — increases cross-region egress and costs. We measured a 3x token rate on warmups last time this happened.
Jen: Policy change came from compliance to reduce blast radius after recent audit. We can add scoped allowlists but need an audit trail for exceptions. Prefer short-lived service-account-based allowances.
Marta: Quick check: our bootstrap calls to KMS use role arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/gpu-bootstrap-role and hit KMS in eu-west-2. Let me paste the minimal SG rule we need.
Marta: ```
# allow bootstrap -> kms
- cidr: 10.64.0.0/16
  to: kms.eu-west-2.amazonaws.com
  ports: [443]
  comment: gpu-bootstrap-kms
```
Kai: That looks right. If we add that single allow it should be narrow enough. Also image pulls come from ecr.eu-west-2.amazonaws.com via NAT gw, which would still be blocked by new egress default unless we allow the NAT gateway subnets.
Jen: We can approve a short-lived exception for the bootstrap role + NAT subnet egress to ECR, but we need an audit entry: who approved, expiration, and linked ticket. Can infra open a PR that references the JIRA?
Marta: I'll open INFRA-9287 with the exact rules and TTL (48h). Suggest we coordinate a canary: enable policy for 10% of subnets first.
Oliver: Canary is good. I'll add a monitor to watch Pending->Running latency and GPU pool capacity. Alert if Pending replicas > 3 for > 10m.
deploy-bot: deploy scheduled: fw-policy/eu-west-2 -> apply (canary target 2 subnets) @Jen requested. ID: db-2026-03-20-07
Kai: If the canary looks clean, we still need to watch for audit log volume: allowing KMS will increase KMS->CloudTrail events. That could spike our log ingestion costs in the short window. Anyone have a quick estimate?
Marta: Rough calc — bootstrap calls ~0.8 requests/node for first minute. If we spin up 150 new nodes during the window that's ~120 extra KMS calls, not huge. But image pull logs and STS assume role events will be bigger.
Jen: Ok, given numbers that's acceptable. Request: all exceptions auto-expire and we create an alert on CloudTrail anomalous source IPs for the window.
Oliver: Added a dashboard panel: "gpu.provision.pending_count" and a cheap CloudWatch alarm. Will also capture cross-region egress bytes to monitor cost leakage.
Marta: PR opened: https://git.company/infra/fw-rules/pulls/421 — includes rule, TTL 48h, canary subnet list, JIRA INFRA-9287. Please review / approve.
Jen: Reviewing now. I will approve once the PR adds the audit tags and the expiration hook.
Kai: Thanks. If anyone from oncall sees spikes after the flip, ping me and I'll trigger a rollback in the firewall controller. :thumbsup:
Oliver: Noted. I'll be watching and will escalate to SRE rotation if anything unexpected hits.
Jen: Approved with comment about audit tags. Scheduling change to be kept to canary only until morning.
Marta: Deploying canary in 5. Will post updates.
Kai: Thanks — keep logs clipped and let's avoid a big cross-region bill.
Marta: Canary applied. Nodes in canary subnets started booting, 6 -> Running within 90s. No errors yet.
Oliver: Monitoring shows no Pending drift and egress bytes stable.
Jen: Audit trail recorded, exception expires in 48h. Closing ticket on my side unless we need extension.
Marta: Rolling to remaining subnets in 30m if no regressions.
Kai: Great job team.
